content:
**Progress M-14M** (Russian: *Прогресс М-14М*), also known as **Progress 46** or **46P** in NASA's numbering system, was an uncrewed Russian cargo spacecraft that resupplied the **International Space Station (ISS)** in 2012. It was part of the **Progress-M 11F615A60** series, an upgraded version of the Soviet-era Progress spacecraft. Below is a detailed overview of its mission:

---

### **Key Details**
- **Mission Name:** Progress M-14M (Progress 46 / 46P)
- **Spacecraft Type:** Progress-M (11F615A60)
- **Launch Date:** **January 25, 2012, 23:06:40 UTC**
- **Launch Site:** **Baikonur Cosmodrome, Site 1/5 (Gagarin's Start)**
- **Launch Vehicle:** **Soyuz-U (11A511U)**
- **Docking Date:** **January 28, 2012, 00:09 UTC**
- **Docking Port:** **Pirs module (nadir port)**
- **Undocking Date:** **April 19, 2012, 11:04 UTC**
- **Deorbit Date:** **April 28, 2012, ~12:40 UTC**
- **Reentry:** **Controlled destructive reentry over the Pacific Ocean**
- **Mission Duration:** **84 days (docked for 81 days)**

---

### **Mission Objectives**
1. **Resupply the ISS** with:
   - **Dry cargo** (food, scientific equipment, spare parts, clothing, etc.)
   - **Propellant** (for station reboost and attitude control)
   - **Water** (for the crew)
   - **Oxygen & air** (for cabin repressurization)
2. **Perform ISS reboosts** to adjust its orbit.
3. **Dispose of waste** by loading trash before undocking and burning up in the atmosphere.

---

### **Cargo Manifest**
Progress M-14M carried approximately **2,669 kg (5,884 lbs)** of supplies, broken down as follows:
- **Dry Cargo:** ~1,350 kg (2,976 lbs)
  - Food rations
  - Scientific experiments (including **BAR experiment** for studying cosmic ray impacts)
  - Spare parts & maintenance tools
  - Personal items for the crew (Expedition 30)
- **Propellant:** ~870 kg (1,918 lbs) for ISS reboosts
- **Water:** ~420 kg (926 lbs) in **Rodnik tanks**
- **Oxygen & Air:** ~50 kg (110 lbs)

---

### **Mission Timeline**
#### **1. Launch & Rendezvous (January 25–28, 2012)**
- Launched on a **Soyuz-U rocket** from Baikonur.
- Followed a **3-day rendezvous profile** (instead of the faster 6-hour profile used in later missions).
- **Automated docking** to the **Pirs module** using the **Kurs-NA** rendezvous system.
- Docking occurred while the ISS was over **Kazakhstan**.

#### **2. Docked Operations (January 28 – April 19, 2012)**
- **Crew unloaded cargo** (Expedition 30: Dan Burbank, Anton Shkaplerov, Anatoly Ivanishin, Oleg Kononenko, André Kuipers, Don Pettit).
- **ISS reboosts** were performed to maintain orbital altitude:
  - **February 15, 2012:** Raised ISS orbit by ~2.5 km using Progress M-14M engines.
  - **March 23, 2012:** Another reboost to prepare for Soyuz TMA-22 landing.
- **Scientific experiments** were conducted, including:
  - **BAR experiment** (studying cosmic ray impacts on electronics).
  - **Molniya-Gamma** (observing terrestrial gamma-ray flashes).

#### **3. Undocking & Deorbit (April 19–28, 2012)**
- **Undocked on April 19, 2012**, to make way for **Progress M-15M**.
- Conducted **9 days of autonomous flight** for the **Radar-Progress experiment** (studying plasma effects from engine burns).
- **Deorbited on April 28, 2012**, burning up over the **south Pacific Ocean**.

---

### **Notable Events & Incidents**
1. **Delayed Launch (Original Plan: October 2011)**
   - Originally scheduled for **October 26, 2011**, but delayed due to the **Progress M-12M (44P) launch failure (August 24, 2011)**.
   - The failure was caused by a **third-stage Soyuz-U rocket malfunction**, leading to a **review of all Soyuz/Progress launches**.
   - Progress M-14M was the **first Progress mission after the failure**, marking a return to flight.

2. **Successful Kurs-NA Test**
   - This was one of the first missions to use the **upgraded Kurs-NA** automated docking system (more efficient than the older Kurs-A).
   - The system performed flawlessly, validating its use for future missions.

3. **Radar-Progress Experiment**
   - After undocking, Progress M-14M spent **9 days in autonomous flight** to study **ionospheric disturbances** caused by its engines (part of the **Radar-Progress** experiment).
   - Data was collected by **Russian ground-based radar stations**.

---

### **Technical Specifications (Progress-M 11F615A60)**
| **Parameter**          | **Value** |
|------------------------|-----------|
| **Length**             | 7.23 m (23.7 ft) |
| **Diameter**           | 2.72 m (8.9 ft) |
| **Mass (Empty)**       | ~7,020 kg (15,476 lbs) |
| **Mass (Loaded)**      | ~7,280 kg (16,050 lbs) |
| **Solar Array Span**   | 10.6 m (34.8 ft) |
| **Power Generation**   | ~1.0 kW (solar arrays) |
| **Propulsion**         | **SKD main engine** (300 kgf thrust) + **DPO thrusters** |
| **Docking Mechanism**  | **SSVP (Androgynous Peripheral Docking System)** |

---

### **Legacy & Significance**
- **First successful Progress mission after the M-12M failure**, restoring confidence in Russian cargo deliveries.
- **Validated the Kurs-NA docking system**, which became standard for future Progress and Soyuz missions.
- **Supported long-duration ISS expeditions** (Expedition 30/31) by delivering critical supplies.
- **Contributed to ISS orbital maintenance** through reboosts.

---
### **Sources & Further Reading**
- **NASA ISS Mission Pages**: [Progress 46 (M-14M) Overview](https://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/station/structure/elements/progress.html)
- **Roscosmos Press Releases** (2012 archives)
- **Spaceflight101**: [Progress M-14M Mission Summary](https://spaceflight101.com/progress-m-14m/)
- **RussianSpaceWeb**: [Progress-M Details](http://www.russianspaceweb.com/progress_m.html)
